title: Two-distance and list-two-distance coloring of cacti: the subcubic case and the C5 obstruction
summary: The square $G^2$ of a graph joins two vertices at distance at most two; a proper coloring of $G^2$ is a 2-distance coloring of $G$. For a cactus $G$ (every edge on at most one cycle) we determine both the 2-distance chromatic number $χ(G^2)$ and the choice number $\mathrm{ch}(G^2)$ exactly: they are always equal, and the common value is $Δ+1$ if $Δ\ge4$, is 4 if $Δ=3$ and $G$ has no block equal to $C_5$, is 5 if $Δ=3$ and $G$ has a $C_5$ block, and is the classical value if $Δ\le2$. For $Δ\ge6$ the value $Δ+1$ is already known, since cacti are outerplanar and hence $K_{2,3}$-minor-free…
